newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will likely refrain from open market operations on Wednesday, analysts said.

"I don't expect anything," said James Glassman, vice president and economist at Chase Securities Inc. "We are entering a period when seasonal reserve needs are large and growing. But the three-day (system) RP (the Fed conducted on Monday) was large. It looks as though the (open market) desk is on top of the reserve situation."
Fed funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent at 1100 EST/1600 GMT, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.

"I'm calling for no Fed intervention, based on the behavior of the funds rate," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co Inc. "The three-day system that's outstanding that the Fed did on Monday is satisfying the add need for today."
"The three-day RP is still in place today and Fed funds are still comfortable so it looks like they don't need to add anymore," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc.
